transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Redwood CSM), Sofia Alvarez (Mediconnex HoMLOps), Kenji Yamamoto (Mediconnex Platform), Liam O'Neill (Mediconnex CTO), Tara Brooks (Mediconnex SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we'll kick off, quick agenda: readout of sprint 2 bench, routing decisions, and next steps. Priya I'll hand off to you for the numbers.
[00:28] Priya: yeah thanks Jordan, hi all. quick caveat — these are lab runs not prod, we used the same seed corpus you provided and the incumbent baseline is the cloud vendor snapshot you shared last week. i'll start with p50, p95 and p99 across the two configs.
[00:53] Priya: Redwood hosted with our LLM-v3-quant profile — p50 38ms, p95 110ms, p99 210ms. incumbent reported p50 78ms, p95 190ms, p99 360ms on their GA endpoint. so the delta is fairly consistent — about 40ms p50 improvement, and notable tail improvement.
[01:23] Sofia: sorry can i jump in — are those numbers with prefix cache warm? like did you pre-seed KV cache?
[01:30] Priya: good question — yes these were with warm kv cache on a per-session basis; we also ran cold runs, cold p50 was roughly 140ms for us and 240ms for incumbent. we'll upload both traces.
[01:50] Kenji: when you say kv cache are you talking about the prefix cache or the token KV cache — sorry sometimes the names get swapped in transcripts i mean the token kv.
[01:58] Priya: token KV cache, right — sorry, kv, as in the key/value attention cache. sometimes fireflies writes it as K V cash in the notes.
[02:10] Liam: what's the model size/quantization there? Q4 int8?
[02:15] Priya: these were fp16 baseline runs for fairness, then we did an int8 quant profile Q3 (our internal naming) to test cost/latency. Q3 int8 gave p50 34ms and p95 95ms — small quality delta on a couple hallucination tests, we flagged those examples.
[02:38] Tara: flagged how bad? like a 10% failure rate on exact-match or just slight token differences?
[02:45] Priya: more like the latter — token ordering/extra stop tokens on 3/300 prompts we used for eval, so ~1% noisy. not systemic, but we recommended keeping fp16 for critical flows and using int8 for low-risk routes.
[03:02] Jordan: ok great— can you show throughput scaling? mediconnex cares about 10k rps headroom.
[03:10] Priya: yes, we ran horizontal scaling on dedicated GPU pools and also a hosted autoscale config. single GPU sustained ~650 rps at target latency SLO (p95 < 150ms). with 16 GPUs (dedicated pool) we hit ~10.4k rps with p95 ~145ms on the pinned-model runs. the incumbent needed roughly 26% more GPU equivalent to hit similar throughput on their reported numbers.
[03:43] Kenji: how are you normalizing GPU equivalence? same instance class?
[03:46] Priya: we normalized by vram + model sharding characteristics and used their public instance spec. it's an approximation — we'll include the normalization spreadsheet in the logs.
[04:00] Marcus: quick note — figures include continuous batching turned on with batch size cap 64 and dynamic batching timeout 8ms; that's how we preserved latency.
[04:13] Sofia: does that mean we can't get lower p50 without higher cost? can batching be tuned per route?
[04:20] Priya: yep, routing by route is supported. low-latency routes we set batch-size 8 and aggressive timeouts which costs more but drops p50 to ~28ms. background or non-interactive routes we batch bigger.
[04:37] Liam: what about fallback behavior if a node is saturated — do we failover to another region/model?
[04:43] Jordan: yes — we propose a routing playbook: primary route to Dedicated pinned model (low-latency), fallback to Hosted cheaper variant, final fallback to incumbent only if all else fails (we can flip that). we monitor token-level errors and automatic rollback.
[05:00] Tara: network-wise, are we seeing cross-region hops in the benchmark? that sometimes skews p99.
[05:06] Priya: all the lab runs were intra-region. for your production we'd recommend co-located infra to avoid added RTT.
[05:18] Sofia: can you share the raw p99 traces? i want to see where tail starts spiking.
[05:21] Priya: yes — uploading them to your S3 bucket after the call.
[05:28] Jordan: quick commercial note — price delta for dedicated capacity is in the matrix i'll send, but to be explicit: dedicated commit buys you 18% lower unit cost at scale vs hosted with burst. Jordan: sorry — that's a typo in my slide, i'll send corrected table.
[05:45] Kenji: any security impacts of pinning models? we need to know audit logs and kms details.
[05:50] Marcus: standard: SOC2 Type II, audit logs per-token routing, optional KMS/HSM integration for private deployments, and VPC peering. we have a security pack we can give you.
[06:05] Tara: does the dedicated option expose model weights to our network — we need to ensure airgap/air-gapped requirements for parts of our stack.
[06:12] Priya: we offer Private on-prem packaging where model artifacts are customer-controlled. for cloud-dedicated the model weights remain encrypted and managed by Redwood; we can discuss on-prem steps if requirements demand.
[06:26] Sofia: switching back to bench: when you ran the incumbent baseline were you on the publicly available endpoint or the negotiated private instance?
[06:34] Priya: the incumbent runs were on the private instance you provided access to — it was a fair comparison.
[06:40] Sofia: good. one concern — our production request distribution includes some long context requests, up to 6k tokens, will your latency keep linear?
[06:49] Priya: latency grows roughly linearly with context length but our kernels have optimizations for attention patterns you described, and the KV caching avoids re-computation for sessioned users, so p95 tails remain reasonable. we'll include a long-context run in the pinned-model test.
[07:10] Kenji: earlier you mentioned prefix caching for conversation state — if we use shard routing that might break cache hits, any workarounds?
[07:18] Priya: good point — we recommend sticky routing for sessioned conversational traffic so KV hits stay local. sticky routing plus node-aware cache replication gives best result; we can demo that in the next run.
[07:33] Jordan: let's do a quick dive into the one failure class you mentioned on int8 — Priya can you play back the two examples?
[07:40] Priya: sure. example one: prompt asked for enumerated business rules, model returned duplicate clause. likely tokenization boundary issue with int8 rounding. example two: minor hallucination on dataset-specific acronym expansion. both recover with fp16.
[08:03] Sofia: that suggests a guardrail: use int8 on non-critical helpers, fp16 on critical decision paths. acceptable.
[08:12] Liam: what about A/B routing to test quality in prod? can we route 5% to int8 and monitor evals?
[08:19] Priya: absolutely — Redwood Console supports canary percentages per route and automated quality monitors tied to prompt eval sets; if the regression crosses threshold we auto-roll back.
[08:31] Kenji: what's the expected effort to enable canary and automated evals?
[08:35] Marcus: from our side it's a week to wire up your evaluation prompts and hook them to the monitoring hooks if you give access. so 5-7 business days.
[08:45] Sofia: timeline — we're hoping to decide on vendor by Thanksgiving. is that feasible?
[08:51] Jordan: yes, if we complete the pinned-model 10k run and provide security docs by next Wednesday we can be ready for procurement review on 2026-11-24.
[09:01] Tara: can you also include a worst-case cost ladder for sudden traffic spikes? we need a headroom plan.
[09:07] Jordan: yes i'll include a burst cost ladder showing cost per token at 2x/3x/5x traffic with autoscale assumptions.
[09:15] Priya: backing to throughput instrumentation — the profiler traces will show batch sizes, batch latencies, and scheduling wait times; that should point where tail originates.
[09:29] Sofia: okay let's move to anomalies — did you see any outlier runs where p99 jumped unexpectedly?
[09:36] Priya: we observed two outlier 1-minute windows where p99 spiked to ~600ms — in both cases there was a concurrent checkpoint/GC on the host in our test harness. different from network spikes. we'll annotate them in the logs.
[09:52] Kenji: is that a scheduling artifact or something inherent to the runtime?
[09:56] Priya: scheduling artifact in our test VM; on dedicated hardware with cgroup pinning it disappears.
[10:05] Liam: curious about model fallback fidelity — if you fall back from pinned fp16 to hosted int8, do you preserve session state?
[10:13] Priya: yes session state is persisted in the prefix store; we convert/normalize tokens so the session remains coherent, but you may see small differences in completions. our playbook allows short user-visible checks to avoid bad UX.
[10:30] Jordan: all right — quick recap of the experimental runs we'll do before next sync: 1) pinned fp16 10k RPS run with long-context (6k tokens) test, 2) pinned int8 Q3 run with canary harness at 5%, 3) dedicated scaling with node pinning to reproduce the two outlier GC spikes, 4) routing stickiness test.
[10:55] Sofia: and please include raw traces and the normalization sheet.
[10:58] Jordan: yes. we'll also put together a decision matrix: cost/latency/quality tradeoffs for the procurement review.
[11:05] Tara: procurement will want the KMS/HSM integration doc and SOC2 evidence.
[11:10] Marcus: i'll attach the latest SOC docs and KMS integration guide.
[11:16] Kenji: one last technical question — for quantization, are you using post-training quantization or QAT?
[11:22] Priya: these were post-training int8 runs. we can explore QAT if you want model-level fine-tuning to recover minor quality regressions, but that's additional work with model owner approvals.
[11:34] Sofia: how much time would QAT add?
[11:36] Priya: usually 2-3 sprints depending on dataset access — roughly 3-6 weeks.
[11:41] Liam: for procurement decision, can you give a one-slide summary of risks for int8?
[11:46] Jordan: yes — we'll add a single-slide risk summary: regression cases, mitigations, canary plans.
[11:52] Jordan: any blockers from your side?
[11:55] Sofia: none — just need the logs and pinned-model run, plus procurement packet.
[12:00] Jordan: great. final quick timeline check: Priya will run bench by 2026-11-20, Jordan will send pricing and cost ladder 2026-11-18, Marcus will share SOC docs today, and we'll meet 2026-11-24 for procurement gate.
[12:18] Marcus: noted. thanks everyone.
[12:22] (end)

Notes: speaker labels mix roles, occasional ASR mistakes (K V cash, Junks), natural crosstalk. Links referenced: /shared/mediconnex/bench-20261117/logs (to be uploaded), /security/soc2/mediconnex-pack.zip (shared by Marcus).
